**Abbott Laboratories (CIK 1800) — major transactions and initiatives affecting FY2024 results** (fiscal year ended December 31, 2024; 10-K filed 2025-02-21, accession 0001628280-25-007110)

**Headline context.** FY2024 net sales were $41.95 billion (fact 1550474) versus $40.11 billion in 2023 (fact 1550465), up 4.6% reported; operating income was $6.825 billion (fact 1545490) and net income $13.402 billion (fact 1544911). The net income figure is heavily influenced by a large non-operating item (see below), so it is not comparable to operating performance.

**1. Divestiture of a non-core Established Pharmaceutical business (Q2 2024).** In the second quarter of 2024 Abbott sold a non-core business in its Established Pharmaceutical Products segment, recording a ~$143 million loss in Other (income) expense, net. The loss included $116 million of cumulative foreign currency translation adjustment reclassified out of AOCI; net assets sold (mainly inventory and net PP&E) had a carrying value of $28 million (Note 4, chunk 1800/abt-20241231:208000; also Note 5, chunk :212800). This is the main reason Other income, net fell to $376 million in 2024 from $479 million in 2023 (chunk :131200).

**2. Restructuring / cost-reduction programs.** In 2024 management approved plans to streamline operations across the Diagnostic, Medical Devices, Established Pharmaceutical and Nutritional businesses, including discontinuation of the ZonePerfect® product line. Abbott recorded $129 million of employee-related severance and other charges ($62M cost of products sold, $21M R&D, $46M SG&A), plus $34 million of inventory charges and $12 million of fixed-asset impairments; $32 million was paid in 2024, leaving a $97 million liability (Note 8, chunk :219200). Total restructuring and other cost-reduction charges were ~$185 million in 2024 versus $122 million in 2023 (chunk :283200). The ZonePerfect discontinuation also dampened U.S. Adult Nutritionals sales (chunk :96000).

**3. Impairments.** Intangible assets fell $207 million in 2024 due to impairment charges in cost of products sold, primarily in Medical Devices; IPR&D declined $39 million from an impairment charge in R&D, partly offset by $35 million from finalizing purchase accounting on a prior acquisition (chunk :217600).

**4. Financing and capital-return actions.** On June 26, 2024 Abbott amended its yen term loan, raising principal from ¥59.8bn to ¥92.0bn with maturity extended to June 2029 (~$201 million net proceeds). On November 19, 2024 it repaid €590 million (~$640 million) of 0.10% notes at maturity. On October 11, 2024 the board authorized a new $7 billion share repurchase program. In December 2024 the quarterly dividend was raised 7.3% to $0.59; dividends paid were $3.8 billion in 2024 (chunks :153600, :99200).

**5. Portfolio/operating initiatives.** No material acquisitions closed in 2024 — the CSI ($851 million, April 2023) and Bigfoot (September 2023) deals were 2023 events, with 2024 purchase-accounting finalization only (Note 6, chunk :214400). Growth drivers in 2024 were organic: Medical Devices sales +13.7% ex-FX (CGM $6.4bn, +21.8% ex-FX), Alinity deployment in Core Laboratory, and margin-improvement initiatives lifting gross margin to 50.9% from 50.3%. Partly offsetting: COVID-19 testing sales fell to $747 million from $1.6 billion, and foreign exchange reduced total sales by 2.6% (chunks :113600, :123200, :126400).

**Uncertainty:** the report does not quantify the revenue contribution of the divested business separately, so its sales impact cannot be isolated from the disclosed loss.
